newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products end mixed, gasoline outlook tight.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products end mixed, gasoline outlook tight.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products ended mixed on Tuesday with gasoline tightness still a main feature.
Gasoline was unchanged, at about $211/$213 cif, after crude oil futures snapped back from Monday's sharp sell-off.
But traders said the Med gasoline market was still strong, with no available cargoes and demand seen from Lebanon and other eastern Med destinations.
A 30,000 tonne cargo was rumoured to have been sold from NWE to the Med, but this was not confirmed.
Demand from Nigeria for cat gas was also expected to pick up after it has been absent for the last several months.
Gas oil was stronger, bolstered by firm premiums and stronger IPE gas oil futures.

Russian material was pegged near cif high quotes +50 cents to $1, marginally up from Monday but showing signs of further gains. Dealers said tightness was seen for the first week of March out of the Black Sea with a couple of interested buyers.
FOD heating oil held on to strong premiums talked on Monday when a March 6-8 Italian cargo sold at high fob quotes +$3.75.
High sulphur fuel oil was notionally weaker again despite stronger crude oil futures as prices in northwest Europe fell.
But the market was relatively quiet.
Small requirements were seen into Italy for bunker quality.

High sulphur straight-run cargoes were scarce in the Black Sea but dealers said they saw availabilities of Arabian and Mersin material, the latter heard to be on offer at around $5 a tonne over the quoted cif high.
Low sulphur fuel oil was little changed and physical offers into Italy were pegged at around $105/$106 cif Italy.
Naphtha prices were unchanged at a notional $200/$205 cif.
Sluggish end-user demand was balanced by speculation that several traders, while discouraged by rich freight rates, were trying to co-load cargoes to ship to the firm Far East market.
